entry.title: Verifiable Settlement and Pricing for Local Energy Markets: Architecture and Deployment on Hyperledger Besu
entry.summary:
We implement privacy-preserving local electricity exchanges using an automated market maker on the Hyperledger Besu network under QBFT consensus. The proposed protocol operator collects individual electricity positions off-chain and publishes aggregate supply and demand on the blockchain, where smart contracts compute market prices every fifteen minutes. Individual positions remain off-chain; Poseidon2 commitments and UltraHonk zeroknowledge proofs, generated from Noir circuits, verify aggregation, payments, and daily balance updates.

Source: arXiv Cryptography & Security (cs.CR) · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #decision-theory #quant-finance

entry.title: How to Defeat a Mafia (of Size 1). The game "Mafia'' is a social deduction game where $n$ players attempt to uncover a covert coalition of $m$ players among the $n$.
entry.summary:
The game "Mafia'' is a social deduction game where $n$ players attempt to uncover a covert coalition of $m$ players among the $n$. Typically, $d=1$ of the non-coalition players are labelled ``Detective'' and have special abilities. Most game-theoretic analysis considers, however, only the variant without a Detective.

Source: arXiv Cryptography & Security (cs.CR) · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #decision-theory

entry.title: Infrastructure for Verifiable AI: Where Proof Costs Go and How Hardware Can Help
entry.summary:
Users of artificial intelligence services, including those powered by large language models and other transformer-based models, need assurance that inference and training follow the declared computation without exposing private models or data. Zero-knowledge proofs can provide this assurance, but proof generation remains expensive. Hardware acceleration research often reports gains for individual cryptographic operations, leaving their effect on the full cost of proving neural-network workloads, particularly large transformer models, unclear.

Source: arXiv Systems & Architecture (cs.OS, cs.AR, cs.NI, cs.PF) · Tags: #computer-architecture #kernel-os #cryptography #ml-theory

entry.title: What Does It Cost to Force-Close a Lightning Channel? Evidence from 974,000 Channel Closes, 2018-2026
entry.summary:
Bitcoin's Lightning payment network returns the funds of a channel that cannot close cooperatively through pre-signed transactions whose fees and delays fall on its operators. That fee design is being replaced: Bitcoin Core 31.0 removed the mempool rule anchor channels relied on, and the Lightning specification adopted zero-fee commitments in May 2026. What the old design costs has never been measured across fee regimes.

Source: arXiv Systems & Architecture (cs.OS, cs.AR, cs.NI, cs.PF) · Tags: #computer-architecture #kernel-os #cryptography #networking

entry.title: Bait: Mitigating Harmful Agentic Reinforcement Learning via Probing Reward Function
entry.summary:
We expose a safety vulnerability on nascent agentic reinforcement-learning-as-a-service. Specifically, with a cost as low as $20, we show that safety alignment of a large language model (e.g., Inkling) can be completely subverted through rounds of harmful agentic reinforcement learning (agentic RL) with a toxic environment from its users. We also demonstrate that upon a successful harmful agentic RL attack via the service API, the attackers can potentially use the safety-degraded model to assist with real-world harmful activities, e.g., exploit software vulnerabilities and launch code re-use attacks.

Source: arXiv Cryptography & Security (cs.CR) · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #ml-theory #infosec

entry.title: Package managers have an integrity problem
entry.summary:
I tested 25 of the most popular package managers to check whether they detect a compromised package repository injecting malicious code into legitimate packages. This code integrity problem could be solved using cryptographic hashes or signatures, but many package managers are still vulnerable to this threat. Of the 25 package managers reviewed 1 , fewer than half used lockfiles that checked for tampering by default, and only two verified the integrity of every package they downloaded.

Source: Trail of Bits Security Research · Tags: #infosec #cryptography #rust #databases

entry.title: Connecting Cryptanalytic Distinguishers through Divisibility
entry.summary:
Integral distinguishers can reveal more than a zero-sum property: the number of ones in an output component may be divisible by a high power of $2$, rather than merely being even. To exploit this divisibility, we relate linear, integral, differential-linear, and restricted differential sums through two-way conversions with explicit divisibility guarantees and data complexity, recovering established links as special cases. We derive exact random-permutation probabilities and rigorous bounds to quantify the distinguishing strength while accounting for dependencies between output conditions.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #infosec

entry.title: Just How Secure is SRP, Really?
entry.summary:
An asymmetric Password-Authenticated Key Exchange (aPAKE) protocol allows a client and a server to agree upon a cryptographic key, with the only information shared in advance being a low-entropy password (memorized by the client) and a corresponding password file (stored in the server). The standard security definition for aPAKE is in the Universally Composable (UC) framework. Since aPAKE does not rely on a PKI, such protocols have received much attention in recent years due to their potential of replacing the traditional “password-over-TLS” approach for client-server authentication on the Internet.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #combinatorics

entry.title: One More Pair, More Information Gained: Improved Attacks on LowMC with Full S-box Layers Using Two Plaintext/Ciphertext Pairs
entry.summary:
Motivated by LowMC cryptanalysis challenge, research in recent years focuses more on attacking LowMC in \PICNIC application setting, \ie an attacker can see only a single plaintext/ciphertext pair. It can be noted that in the security proof of \PICNIC, LowMC is required to be secure under two plaintexts, it is thus meaningful to investigate the security of LowMC in this direction. Pioneered by Liu, Isobe and Meier at Crypto 2021, they combined algebraic techniques with difference enumeration attack, which could attack all three 4-round LowMC instances adopting full S-Box layers in \PICNIC with only two chosen plaintexts.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp

entry.title: MODDIV-WC: Unit-Anchored Toeplitz/Hankel Rounding with Exact Binary-LWE Masking and an IND-CCA Security Route
entry.summary:
\begin{abstract} We present MODDIV-WC, a public-key encryption and key-encapsulation candidate based on a widened Hankel linear map followed by deterministic integer division, together with an implicit-rejection Fujisaki--Okamoto wrapper, MODDIV-WC-FO. The construction uses a secret vector whose first coordinate is fixed to one and whose remaining coordinates are sampled from a positive interval. This unit anchor makes the Hankel map surjective for every admissible secret, a property that is central to the proof.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #post-quantum
